text: When the task description does not specify exact formats, schemas, or conventions (input string layouts, column names, path conventions, file encodings), do not invent plausible ones; derive them from the description/examples or test only behaviors the spec explicitly guarantees, since setup failures from guessed formats indicate a wrong fixture, not a wrong implementation.

Assert only properties the specification explicitly guarantees (return types, existence, counts, documented statuses); avoid asserting extra side effects, decorations, exact numeric types, or invariants the description does not require.

When testing error paths, only assert exception types or raising behavior the spec explicitly names and the reference confirms; construct inputs that isolate exactly one error condition and satisfy all other preconditions, and do not assume which validation check takes precedence.

Do not assume edge-case semantics (empty results, NaN for all-non-numeric positions, degenerate cases, which types count as numeric, or randomness being fresh each call) beyond what the description states; derive expected values from the described semantics and examples rather than intuition.

When the spec allows or documents special-case behavior (e.g., single-cluster returning the original image, 'no change' rows for identical files), test that documented behavior rather than assuming it raises or yields an empty/general-case result.

For functions that may block or run long (network/server calls), run them in a background thread with a join timeout and capture exceptions, so a blocking implementation fails cleanly instead of hanging the suite; keep tests self-contained by defining helpers rather than relying on unprovided fixtures.
Do not assume the function creates directories or performs other setup the description does not require; set up required preconditions (like destination directories) in the test yourself.
When the spec says invalid inputs are filtered or deduplicated, verify what counts as valid before using it in tests, and prefer inputs the spec clearly treats as valid.
